FGEN-CTX-G2.title: Riverbend Family Clinic - preparing for your annual physical
FGEN-CTX-G2.text:
RIVERBEND FAMILY CLINIC
Preparing for Your Annual Physical

Thank you for booking your annual physical with Riverbend Family Clinic. This sheet explains how to prepare so your visit runs smoothly. Your visit will be with Dr. Hollis Varga or a member of her care team.

Before your visit
- If your provider ordered fasting bloodwork (such as a lipid panel or fasting glucose), do not eat or drink anything except water for 10 hours before your appointment. Please avoid coffee, including black coffee, and chewing gum during the fasting period. Take your usual medications with water unless your provider has told you otherwise.
- Complete the health history questionnaire in the patient portal at least 2 days before your visit. If you cannot use the portal, arrive 30 minutes early to fill it in on paper.
- Make a list of every medication, vitamin and supplement you take, including the dose.

What to bring
- Photo ID and your current insurance card.
- Your medication list.
- Glasses or hearing aids if you use them.
- Any home blood pressure readings from the last month.

Arriving
Please arrive 15 minutes before your appointment time to check in. If you are more than 15 minutes late, we may need to reschedule you. Parking is available in Lot B behind the building; bring your ticket to the front desk for 2 hours of free validated parking. Street parking on Weller Avenue is metered.

During your visit
Your visit includes a review of your history, vital signs, a physical exam, and any screenings recommended for your age. Flu shots are available at no extra charge during your physical from October through March while supplies last. If you have a specific concern, mention it at check-in so enough time can be set aside; a separate appointment may be needed for complex issues.

After your visit
Lab results are posted to the patient portal, usually within 3 business days. Your provider will message you if anything needs follow-up. Normal results may be posted without a personal note. Follow-up visits can often be done by telehealth.

Cancellations
We ask for at least 24 hours notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. Appointments missed or cancelled with less than 24 hours notice are subject to a $40 missed-appointment fee, which is not covered by insurance.

Billing
Most insurance plans cover one preventive physical per year at no cost to you. Additional services discussed or treated during the visit, such as a new problem or a chronic condition review, may be billed separately and may involve a copay. Questions about coverage should be directed to your insurance company; our billing office can provide the procedure codes.

Front desk hours: Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

FGENH-CTX-G1.title: Condo association board meeting minutes
FGENH-CTX-G1.text:
Harbor Point Condominium Association - Board Meeting Minutes
Date: Thursday, September 24
Location: Community room, Building B
Present: Linda Marsh (President), Owen Castellano (Treasurer), Priya Nair (Secretary), Hal Jensen, Beatriz Soto. Also present: Renee Okoro (property manager, Seaside Management) and 11 owners.
Quorum confirmed. Meeting called to order at 7:02 pm.

1. Approval of August minutes
Approved unanimously without changes.

2. Treasurer's report
Owen Castellano reported the operating account is on budget for the year. The reserve fund balance is $179,500. Delinquent dues stand at three units, total $4,210; the management company has sent second notices.

3. Building A elevator
The Building A elevator has been out of service intermittently since July because of a failing controller. Two quotes were received. The board voted 4-1 (Jensen opposed) to accept the Carver Lift Services quote of $38,500 to replace the controller, paid from the reserve fund. Carver estimates the work takes six to eight weeks once parts arrive; parts are on order and no arrival date has been given. Renee Okoro will post updates in the lobby and by email.

4. Roof replacement, Buildings A and B
Three bids were reviewed for full roof replacement on both buildings:
- Kessler Roofing: $212,000
- Summit Exteriors: $236,500
- Delgado & Sons: $249,000
The board voted unanimously to move forward with Kessler Roofing, subject to reference checks and a signed contract. A start date will be negotiated after the contract is signed. The treasurer noted that after the elevator payment the reserve fund cannot cover the full roof cost. A special assessment across all 64 units was discussed at length. Several owners asked for a payment plan option. The motion on a special assessment was tabled to the October 22 meeting, pending an updated reserve study. No assessment amount was agreed.

5. Pet policy
The board voted 5-0 to remove the 35-pound weight limit for dogs. The limit of two pets per unit is unchanged. All pets, including existing ones, must be registered with the management office using the new form, with proof of rabies vaccination for dogs and cats. Registration deadline: November 15.

6. Guest parking
The old paper guest passes are being retired because of misuse. Each unit will receive two numbered hang-tag guest passes. Renee Okoro will order the passes and distribute them to units by October 10. Vehicles in guest spaces without a hang-tag after October 10 may be towed after one warning sticker.

7. Open forum
Owners raised noise from the pool pump at night (management to check timer), a request for a second bike rack by Building B (board to get a price), and a question about EV charging (no action; to be revisited in spring).

Action items
- Renee Okoro: sign Carver contract; order guest hang-tags and distribute by October 10; post elevator updates.
- Owen Castellano: request updated reserve study before October 22.
- Priya Nair: circulate new pet registration form to all owners by October 1.
- Linda Marsh: contact Kessler references.

Next meeting: Thursday, October 22, 7 pm, community room.
Adjourned 8:41 pm.

Trail conditions

- Sunday, October 18: Hemlock Meadow family walk, 3 miles, easy. Dogs on leash welcome.
- Saturday, October 31: Full moon night hike, 4 miles. Headlamps required. Limited to 15 people; sign up on the club board.

PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

FGEN-CTX-I1.title: Sourdough starter feeding schedule
FGEN-CTX-I1.text:
SOURDOUGH STARTER - FEEDING SCHEDULE

Day 1: Mix 50 g whole wheat flour with 50 g lukewarm water in a clean jar. Cover loosely and leave at room temperature, ideally 24 to 26 C.

Day 2: You may see a few bubbles or nothing at all. Both are normal. Leave it alone.

Days 3 to 6: Once a day, discard all but 50 g of the starter, then add 50 g flour (half whole wheat, half white) and 50 g water. Stir well and mark the level on the jar with a rubber band.

Days 7 onward: Switch to two feedings a day, about 12 hours apart. A healthy starter should roughly double within 4 to 8 hours of feeding and smell pleasantly sour, like yogurt.

Troubleshooting
- Grey liquid on top ("hooch") means it is hungry. Pour it off and feed.
- No rise after day 10: move it somewhere warmer and use more whole wheat flour.
- Pink or orange streaks: throw it out and start again.

Storage
Once established, keep it in the fridge and feed once a week. Take it out the night before baking and give it two room-temperature feedings before mixing dough.

items.question: I'm trying to decide between leasing a new car and buying a used one. I drive about 8,000 miles a year, I have about 6,000 saved, and I really hate dealing with repairs. Walk me through the trade-offs and tell me which way you'd lean.
items.answer:
At 8,000 miles a year, you're a low-mileage driver, which is the key fact here. Leasing is usually priced around 10,000 to 12,000 miles a year, so you'd be paying for miles you won't use, and you'd still have a monthly payment forever with nothing to show at the end. Buying used means the car is yours once it's paid off, and at your mileage a well-chosen used car can last many years. The catch is repairs, which you hate. That's the real trade-off: a lease keeps you under warranty the whole time, while a used car eventually falls out of warranty and you're the one handling it.

With about 6,000 saved, I'd lean toward buying used, but a specific kind of used car: something a few years old, low miles, and with a reputation for reliability, ideally still under some factory warranty. Put your savings toward the down payment and keep a few thousand aside as a repair fund, so a surprise doesn't wreck you. If the idea of any repair at all is genuinely unbearable, a lease on a low-mileage plan can make sense, but you're paying a premium for that peace of mind and you'll never own anything.

items.question: I have to give a two minute toast at my brother's wedding on Saturday. Help me write the opening.
items.answer:
I don't have any details about your brother or his partner, so I can't write the personal parts for you. But here's an opening shape that works, with the blanks being things only you know:

"Good evening, everyone. For those who don't know me, I'm [name], [brother's name]'s brother. I've known him longer than almost anyone in this room, which means I've also had the longest front-row seat to the person he's become. And I have to say, watching him meet [partner's name] has been one of the best things I've ever seen."

From there, one specific memory of the two of them, then a short wish for their marriage. The key is to keep it to one story, not three, and to say the partner's name early so it doesn't feel like a speech about your brother alone.

items.question: Okay, settle this for us. Is a hot dog a sandwich?
items.answer: Honestly, it depends on the definition you pick. If a sandwich is just filling between two pieces of bread, then yes, a hot dog qualifies. But if the bun has to be two separate slices, then no, because a hot dog bun is one piece hinged together. So I'd say it's a sandwich by the loose definition, and its own thing by the strict one.
